newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher along with natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher along with natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures hit new highs again Friday, drawing strength from expected winter demand and following the lead of natural gas futures, industry sources said.
"There has been lots of focus on the Henry Hub natural gas contracts," said one Houston-based futures broker.
November natural gas futures expired up 16.7 cents at $2.652 per mmBtu on Friday, and traders said the increase had a psychological impact on power.
November electricity futures expire on Monday, and traders said the contracts were expected to show more upside then, with expectations of strengthening demand due to approaching winter demand.
"We may not see as much action in the November contract, but remaining months could move higher," the Houston-based broker said.

November California-Oregon Border (COB) settled up $1.03 at $21.28 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract high of $21.75, while December closed up 68 cents at $21.33 after hitting a new contract high of $21.50.
January COB also hit a new contract high of $20.50 on Friday, and ended up 64 cents at $20.25 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds were steady to $1.15 higher.
November Palo Verde (PV) ended up 57 cents at $19.50 per MWh after hitting a new contract high of $20.25, while December ended down 10 cents at $18.70 after trade as high as $19.50 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds were steady to 20 cents higher.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 431 COB and 204 PV contracts traded Friday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
